video_title: NEAR Just Got Its First ETF. What Happens Next?
gist: Bankless host David talks with Sal (Sovereign) and Hunter (Bitwise) about Bitwise's new NEAR ETF (NRR), which drew about $50M of inflows in its first three days, and about NEAR's investment case. The case rests on NEAR Intents revenue (>$32B volume, rising take rates, buybacks held rather than burned), a proposed cut in inflation, a cheap valuation versus AI startups (~$5B cap), and a world of many models and many chains plus enterprise demand for private AI inference.

themes.theme: Bitwise NRR ETF launch and flows

insights.claim: Bitwise's NEAR ETF (ticker NRR) took in roughly $50 million of inflows in its first three days, i.e. over $10 million per day, with daily trading volume of $10-20 million.
insights.speaker: Hunter (Bitwise)
insights.so_what: Strong early flows create a new structural bid for NEAR from TradFi wallets; track whether daily creations persist.
insights.quote: in the first three days, I I I think uh something like 50 million of inflows into NR

insights.claim: Hunter says NRR's launch has been extraordinarily strong versus other single-asset crypto ETFs launched in 2026, noting that assets with larger market caps traded less volume and drew smaller inflows at their ETF launches.
insights.speaker: Hunter (Bitwise)
insights.so_what: Relative ETF demand is a signal of which alt narratives (AI) resonate with mainstream allocators.
insights.quote: there are assets with larger market caps that are trading less volume and have had less inflows

insights.claim: The NRR ETF handles staking on investors' behalf, so holders get staking yield without making their own staking decisions.
insights.speaker: Hunter (Bitwise)
insights.so_what: Staking inside the wrapper makes the ETF a yield-bearing product, improving its appeal against spot-only alt ETFs.

insights.claim: Bitwise's involvement with NEAR predates the ETF: it published institutional valuation research over a year ago, launched a European NEAR ETP, runs what it believes is the fourth-largest NEAR validator, and operates MPC infrastructure for NEAR Intents and chain signatures.
insights.speaker: Hunter (Bitwise)
insights.so_what: The issuer is also network infrastructure, which ties its commercial incentives to NEAR's success and makes continued marketing likely.
insights.quote: I believe um the fourth largest validator uh on uh on Near

insights.claim: Hunter argues a successful ETF launch is possible even in a bear market, citing the Bitwise Hyperliquid (HYPE) ETF, and says current timing benefits from improving sentiment while Bitcoin remains meaningfully below its all-time high.
insights.speaker: Hunter (Bitwise)
insights.so_what: Suggests alt-ETF demand is driven more by narrative fit than by the overall cycle phase.
insights.quote: it it's possible to have a successful uh ETF launch even in a bare market

insights.claim: Sal says he hopes NRR will pass $100 million and eventually $1 billion in AUM.
insights.speaker: Sal (Sovereign)
insights.so_what: These are the AUM milestones to watch as a gauge of sustained institutional demand for NEAR.
insights.quote: I look forward to seeing it break 100 million and then ultimately a billion AUM

insights.claim: NEAR Intents has processed more than $32 billion in volume and is raising take rates on transactions, much as a centralized exchange would, to grow both gross fees and net revenue retained by the protocol.
insights.speaker: Sal (Sovereign)
insights.so_what: Rising take rates on growing volume make protocol revenue the main fundamental driver to model for NEAR.
insights.quote: we process more than 32 billion in volume on the system and are starting to scale the take rates

insights.claim: Net revenue from NEAR Intents funds buybacks of NEAR tokens, which go into a permanent capital vehicle rather than being burned (unlike Hyperliquid's burn model). Sal says calling this 'deflationary' is technically inaccurate and Sovereign will correct its report.
insights.speaker: Sal (Sovereign)
insights.so_what: The buybacks reduce circulating supply but the tokens are not destroyed; governance could later burn them or redeploy them as incentives.
insights.quote: driving buybacks of Near tokens that are held in a permanent capital vehicle um and not being burned today to be clear

insights.claim: A NEAR governance-forum proposal would cut NEAR inflation from 2.5% to 1.6% on a two-year linear curve. A second phase would study whether NEAR could ever become a fixed-supply asset, with buyback revenue paying for economic security.
insights.speaker: Sal (Sovereign)
insights.so_what: Lower issuance plus buybacks improves the token's supply/demand balance; watch the governance vote.
insights.quote: reducing inflation from 2.5% to 1.6% 6% over a two-year linear curve

insights.claim: NEAR Intents recently added about 400 tokenized equity products via Ono, so users can swap between any digital asset and any tokenized stock. Wallets such as Ledger and Zcash-ecosystem providers distribute it B2B, and it has a first-party app at near.com.
insights.speaker: Sal (Sovereign)
insights.so_what: Tokenized equities and wallet integrations widen the volume funnel that feeds NEAR's fees.
insights.quote: with the introduction of Ono and 400 tokenized equity products

insights.claim: Sal says Intents volume is currently driven by humans, and expects AI agents to scale it not linearly but on a roughly 10x multiplier.
insights.speaker: Sal (Sovereign)
insights.so_what: Agentic transaction flow is the upside optionality not yet priced into current Intents revenue.
insights.quote: this scales not on a linear basis, but on a you know 10x multiplier outcome

insights.claim: Hunter says 2026 investors have matured past 'eyeballs'-style metrics and now look for revenue-like value capture (such as buybacks), much as internet investors moved from page views to ARPU and retention.
insights.speaker: Hunter (Bitwise)
insights.so_what: Tokens with real revenue and buybacks should get a premium as investors judge crypto on fundamentals.

insights.claim: Hunter argues that at roughly a $5 billion market cap, NEAR may be the cheapest thing a mainstream investor has seen next to AI platforms with traction, at about a tenth of their average valuation.
insights.speaker: Hunter (Bitwise)
insights.so_what: Re-rating NEAR against AI private-market comps rather than other L1s suggests large upside if that frame catches on.
insights.quote: it might be the cheapest thing you've ever seen in your life

insights.claim: Sal notes that in the last 12 months, pre-product AI startups with similar intellectual talent to NEAR's core contributors raised at post-money valuations of $2-3 billion, which is roughly where NEAR traded four months ago.
insights.speaker: Sal (Sovereign)
insights.so_what: AI venture valuations set a floor for how investors may price NEAR as an AI asset.
insights.quote: raising pre-product pre-odel on the AI side at similar valuations to what near was traded 4 months ago

insights.claim: Earlier in 2026 Sal said NEAR was 2-4x underpriced on human adoption alone, before any AI-agent upside. The host says NEAR has since moved from about a dollar and change to just under $5.
insights.speaker: David (host)
insights.so_what: Sal's earlier call has proven right, which adds weight to Sovereign's framework for valuing NEAR.
insights.quote: near is 2 to 4x underpriced at current human level of human levels of adoption

insights.claim: Hunter says the market has moved past the 'CoinMarketCap era': new mainstream investors do not rank crypto assets by market-cap ladder but by how well they connect to themes they care about, mainly AI.
insights.speaker: Hunter (Bitwise)
insights.so_what: Assets with a narrative legible to TradFi (AI) may outperform regardless of where they sit in crypto rankings.
insights.quote: we've moved on from the coin market cap era

insights.claim: Bitwise pitches NEAR to mainstream investors as a blockchain created by a co-inventor of the LLM (Ilia) that lets both humans and AI agents use AI and move assets across chains, which needs no deep crypto knowledge.
insights.speaker: Hunter (Bitwise)
insights.so_what: A simple AI-linked story widens the pool of buyers for NEAR beyond crypto natives.
insights.quote: the co-inventor of LLM has created a a blockchain

insights.claim: Hunter says the theme of 2026 is that investors have become comfortable with Bitcoin and are looking beyond it for other exposures, with NEAR a first-class candidate.
insights.speaker: Hunter (Bitwise)
insights.so_what: Flows rotating into alt ETFs after Bitcoin could favor a few narrative-driven assets.
insights.quote: the theme of 2026 is that investors have gotten comfortable with Bitcoin and are looking uh beyond Bitcoin

themes.theme: Fragmentation thesis: many models, many chains

insights.claim: Hunter believes both crypto and AI are heading toward fragmentation: many models and agents, multiple L1s and multiple stablecoins. He says NEAR has positioned itself as the simplifying layer that lets humans and agents move across them.
insights.speaker: Hunter (Bitwise)
insights.so_what: Interoperability and routing layers capture value in a multi-chain, multi-model world rather than a winner-take-all one.
insights.quote: the trend across both crypto and AI is going to be fragmentation

insights.claim: The host cites Alex Atallah of OpenRouter, whose company exited for $7 billion according to the host, as proof that the bet on a diversity of models rather than one 'God model' from OpenAI or Anthropic paid off.
insights.speaker: David (host)
insights.so_what: Model-routing businesses are getting large valuations, which supports the multi-model thesis behind NEAR AI.
insights.quote: he exited his company for $7 billion

insights.claim: Hunter argues crypto investors consistently underestimate the importance of team and execution. He contrasts NEAR, a technology build led by Ilia and leaders like Sal, with building 'digital gold', and says it should be judged like a venture-backed AI company.
insights.speaker: Hunter (Bitwise)
insights.so_what: Judging team dynamism, not just tokenomics, is the right lens for tech-platform tokens.
insights.quote: one that is constantly underestimated in the crypto space by investors is the importance of the team

themes.theme: Private AI inference and enterprise demand

insights.claim: Sal sees enterprises adopting tiered AI setups: frontier models for non-sensitive tasks, and open-source models in confidential computing (such as NEAR AI private inference) for sensitive or PII workloads. A router/gateway layer on top would enforce policy and improve AI ROI.
insights.speaker: Sal (Sovereign)
insights.so_what: Heterogeneous model use creates demand for confidential inference infrastructure beyond the frontier labs.
insights.quote: you're seeing the emergence of kind of these tiered structures that are leveraging frontier intelligence for tasks that are not

insights.claim: Sal says enterprises woke up to IP and data-confidentiality concerns about frontier models during Q2-Q3 2026, which boosted the case for NEAR AI's user-owned, sovereign model control.
insights.speaker: Sal (Sovereign)
insights.so_what: Enterprise privacy concerns are a fresh demand catalyst for NEAR AI products.
insights.quote: the enterprise market woke up and started to get concerned around IP and kind of data confidentiality

insights.claim: NEAR AI private inference hosts the widely adopted open-source models with verifiable privacy: clients can run a verifier to prove there is no telemetry and no data leakage. Sal predicts this kind of guaranteed-privacy architecture will be a basic enterprise requirement within two or three years.
insights.speaker: Sal (Sovereign)
insights.so_what: If verifiable privacy becomes mandatory, NEAR AI could tap a large enterprise inference market.
insights.quote: can run a verifier and prove that there's no telemetry and no data leakage

insights.claim: Sal cites Google Trends data showing searches for 'privacy' at a multiple of any previous peak in 30 years, a curve he says looks like the parabolic growth in NEAR Intents volume. Hunter suggests LLM data anxieties may be producing a real, not just stated, shift in consumer preference for privacy.
insights.speaker: Sal (Sovereign)
insights.so_what: A real shift in privacy demand would favor confidential-compute and privacy-chain assets.
insights.quote: privacy is at a multiple of any other peak in search trends

insights.claim: Sal says that Ilia, years before NEAR's mainnet, warned that centralized, oligopolistic frontier AI would not lead to a good outcome. That view underpins NEAR's push for decentralized, privacy-preserving, user-sovereign AI for individuals, businesses and nations.
insights.speaker: Sal (Sovereign)
insights.so_what: Gives NEAR a long-standing, credible narrative against centralized AI that fits the current concerns about AI concentration.
